title: Pauser can sandwich pause/unpause cycles to lock specific stakers into pauseWithdraw (forfeiting rewards) while others claim normally — selective denial of yield
rootCause: Pauser has unilateral, unbounded pause/unpause power with no time-bounds, quorum, or reason field. While paused, stake/withdraw/claim revert; pauseWithdraw works (forfeits rewards per DEDUP-011). Coordinated pause cycles can selectively benefit pauser-aligned stakers.
impactSummary: Strategic Pauser actions can: (a) pause after a collectReward injection so accStablePerShare grows during pause, then unpause to allow aligned stakers to claim first; (b) pause during a user's exit window, forcing them to forfeit rewards via pauseWithdraw.
preservedDetails: ECON-012 carries the game-theory framing of pauser-as-yield-arbiter and the cross-amplifier link with DEDUP-011.
remediation: Allow `claim` during pause for users whose stake predates the pause; enforce a minimum unpause-cooldown; multisig/timelock on the Pauser role at the sibling layer.
dedupNotes: Borderline — relies on Pauser acting adversarially or colluding, which conflicts with profile §6 trust framing. Likely demoted to QA / centralization-report. Kept as a finding because it specifically demonstrates an economic exploitation pattern of an otherwise-documented trust assumption.
